label: Scoped lookup neutralizes cross-packet scaffold contamination but is opt-in, unengaged by any default invocation, and cannot suppress in-scope self-matches: unscoped 'review the acceptance criteria before closeout' returned 20 docs at 0.88 (rc 0), the same prompt scoped to backfilled packet 007 returned 0 (rc 1), track-scoped returned 2 in-track AC docs at 0.88, and scoped to an unbackfilled packet returned that packet's own spec.md at 0.88; the filter is a folder-prefix membership test and every documented invocation is unscoped, so scope adoption is a caller-side mitigation while the residue is the backfill.

WS1-WS4 reconciliation: the review's remediation list and this run's hardening shortlist are additive, not conflicting. WS1 (R1-P1-001) independently verified: default PHASE_COUNT=3, recipe uses bare create.sh --phase then git mv and bare create.sh --phase --parent without path or phase names. WS2 aligns with this run's canon-drift and class-visibility findings under the byte-pin and frozen-array pre-conditions. WS3's control-byte and sub-folder-test items are net-new; R2-P2-004 is this run's three-literal coupling; the union is a superset whose only integration constraint is that the review's 'guard that fails loudly on drift' must not abort scaffold (advisory-only invariant). WS4 has no overlap. Stance difference only: review defers the ~195-spec backfill, this run recommends an operator-run dry-run-first backfill, and f-iter008-001 shows scoping does not remove the self-match reason for it.

Index drift refresh: the committed artifact is unchanged (3,795,532 bytes, mtime 2026-10-06 23:27, phrases['feature specification'] length 199, phrases['acceptance criteria'] length 360, matching iteration 7) while specs/**/spec.md carriers of the template phrase now number 207 against 200 measured at iteration 7; absent carriers are roughly 12 (upper bound, generator exclusions not re-read) and grew ~7 files in one interval, so the absence of a regeneration cadence, not a one-off gap, is the defect.

The lookup's scope filter is a folder-prefix membership test, so scoping can only exclude documents outside the scope and can never neutralize an in-scope document whose indexed phrases match; cross-packet noise reduction is the ceiling of a scoping-based fix.

WS1 spot-check reproduced: default PHASE_COUNT=3, recipe uses bare create.sh --phase, git mv into child 001, and final create.sh --phase --parent with no path; the collision the review describes is real.
